chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Hamzah ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'Two just men from you or two others from non-you.'
He said, then he said: 'The two from you are two Muslims, and the two from non-you are from the People of the Book.'

He said: 'And that is only if a Muslim man dies in a foreign land, and he seeks two Muslim men to bear witness to his will, but does not find two Muslims; then he bears witness to his will with two non-Muslims from the People of the Book who are reputable among their people.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the valid witnesses for a Muslim's will if no Muslims are available?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific context of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:182, distinguishing between the general rule of two just Muslims and the exception for Muslims dying in foreign lands (Arḍ al-Ghurba) where no Muslims are available. In such cases, two reputable People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) may serve as witnesses, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of pragmatic adaptability in diaspora contexts while maintaining the integrity of the testimony through their standing among their own community.
